Maya — attaching the diagram and a short writeup here. Summary below, full details in the attached PNG and export bundle.

Summary: 
- Ingress: Customer requests arrive via our public API endpoint in the regulated US region (us-west-2). Requests are validated and placed into a short-lived in-memory queue (max 60s) and then routed to the inference runtime.
- Transient stores: we use encrypted ephemeral buckets for batch restarts (S3 with SSE-KMS, lifecycle 1 day) — these are not used for long-term retention of PII.
- Pseudonymization: Before any long-term object storage, PII fields flagged by tokenization rules are replaced with cryptographic pseudonyms (HMAC with per-customer salt derived from KMS). The original raw payload is deleted from transient buffers after pseudonymization.
- Long-term artifacts: model logs and prompts are stored in pseudonymized form; raw request artifacts are retained 24 hours for debugging.
- Access controls: IAM roles separated by privilege tier: audit_readonly, svc_inference, platform_admin. Only svc_inference can see full pseudonymized blobs; platform_admins require MFA + approval for key unwrap.

Attachments included: redaction-diagram-v1.drawio.png, redwood-evidence-exports-2026-04-16.zip (logs & access CSV)

Inline answers to SSQ fields (partial):
- Named service accounts (prod): svc-inference-prod@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com; svc-data-ops-prod@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- Log export: filtered audit trail for bh-ORG-2048, CSV of actions for KMS decrypts and object list attached in the zip.
- Cross-border routing: none for this tenant; documented in section 3.2 of the attached diagram.
